chapter: Life in Columbus and recent activity
title: Local work and clinics at Capital

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: So he's still travelling. I guess pretty active. You said you don't do too much local work here in Columbus because the money is generally not good.
No, the scale is all right, you know, but the money isn't that great, you know.

Do you do anything with--well obviously you said you were conducting, you had conducting classes that you were taking with the Capital University concert band. Do you do any playing with jazz bands there?

Oh yeah, I do several little clinics, several little seminars with the jazz arts group. Then with the small group and of course the jazz arts group is the big band, and the fusion band. I did a couple of little things there with them, you know.
Good, good, you know, all of it's good music if the charts are good, you know, and, especially during I've sit on a lot of their recitals, you know, the junior

recitals, senior recitals, sit in with them, you know, which is a very big kick to me. And I stay busy over there doing that a lot of times. Doing those little recitals, seminars, clinics. I enjoy that.
